# How to point the CLI at a different endpoint

This guide shows how to send `glassfrog` commands to a non-production GlassFrog endpoint — for a single command, or persistently for a directory or your whole account.

By default the CLI uses the built-in base URL `https://glassfrog.com/api/v5`. You can override it from three sources, which the CLI consults in this precedence: the `--base-url` flag wins over the `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` environment variable, which wins over the `base_url` key in a `.glassfrogrc` file, which wins over the default. For the full rules, see [Base URL Resolution Reference](../../reference/base-url-resolution.md).

## Prerequisites

- The `glassfrog` CLI is installed.
- The endpoint you want to use, as an absolute URL with an `http` or `https` scheme (for example `https://staging.example.com/api/v5`). A value without a scheme (such as `api.glassfrog.com`) is rejected.

## Steps

Pick the approach that matches how long the override should last.

### Option A — Override for a single command (`--base-url` flag)

Pass the endpoint with the `--base-url` flag on the command that makes the API call:

```
glassfrog --base-url https://staging.example.com/api/v5 <command>
```

The flag overrides every other source — the environment variable, any `.glassfrogrc`, and the default — and applies only to that one invocation.

### Option B — Override for your shell session or account (environment variable)

Export `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` so it applies to every command in the session:

```
export GLASSFROG_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com/api/v5
glassfrog <command>
```

A non-empty value wins over any `.glassfrogrc` and the default. An empty or whitespace-only value is ignored, and the CLI falls through to the configuration file or default.

### Option C — Override per directory or per user (`.glassfrogrc`)

Add a `base_url` key to a `.glassfrogrc` file. The CLI reads the nearest `.glassfrogrc` walking up from the current directory, then the home-directory file as a fallback — so a project-local file takes precedence over your home file.

```
# .glassfrogrc
base_url=https://staging.example.com/api/v5
```

Notes:

- Only full-line `#` comments are recognized. A trailing `# …` on the `base_url` line becomes part of the value.
- A `.glassfrogrc` with no `base_url` entry is skipped — the CLI continues to the home file or the default.
- The same file may also hold your `token`; the CLI never exposes the token when resolving the base URL.

## Verify

Run the command and confirm it reaches the intended endpoint. The CLI does **not** print the resolved base URL or which source won on a successful read — the effective value is used silently, and the source is named only in an error message when resolution fails. Reason about which source should win from the precedence order:

- With the flag set (Option A), the flag wins, and no other source is consulted.
- With `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` set and no flag (Option B), the environment variable wins; the configuration file is not read.
- With only a project-local `.glassfrogrc` (Option C), the value comes from the current directory's file rather than the home file.

To confirm an endpoint is actually in effect, point it at a URL you control (or a deliberately wrong one) and observe where the request lands — a misdirected or unreachable endpoint surfaces as a transport error naming the host. For the same flag value, environment, and filesystem, resolution is deterministic: repeated runs resolve the same value from the same source.

## Troubleshooting

- **The value is rejected as malformed.** The endpoint must be an absolute `http(s)` URL. A scheme-less host (`api.glassfrog.com`), a non-`http` scheme (`ftp://…`), or an unparseable value produces a format error naming the source (the flag, `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL`, or the file path). The CLI does **not** fall through to another source — fix the value at its source.
- **The override seems ignored.** A higher-precedence source is winning. The flag beats the environment variable, which beats the file. If you set `.glassfrogrc` but exported `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL`, the environment variable wins.
- **An empty environment variable.** If `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` is set to an empty or whitespace-only value, it is treated as absent and the CLI uses the next source.
- **A configuration file can't be read or parsed.** If the nearest `.glassfrogrc` exists but cannot be read (e.g. permission denied) or contains a malformed line, the CLI reports a typed error naming that file and does **not** silently fall through to the default.
